findings.title: Windows trailing-dot, trailing-space and 8.3 short-name aliases in protection metadata bypass exclusion and backup protection
findings.reason: key() is lexical only (POSIX normalize, trailing-slash strip, lowercase). The handoff/manifest/lock path patterns accept segments ending in "." or " " and 8.3 short names (e.g. 002-DR~1), which Win32 resolves to the canonical file, but key() maps them to different keys. Schema-valid do_not_read entries spelled this way are silently ignored: restore applied and deleted the excluded backup (orchestrator probe), compact applied on an excluded target and on a nested contracts/** target under a trailing-dot directory exclusion, and context usage still reported an excluded file (adversarial probe). Same class as F22 and the spec.md:150 edge case that Windows aliases must not evade protection.
findings.x-severity: Reviewers disagreed: adversarial P1 (0.90), testing P2 (0.65), security P3 (0.62). Synthesized P2: the impact matches F22, but these spellings do not arise from normal authoring, Node fs returns ENOENT for them so Baton cannot be steered into reading an aliased file, and compaction keeps a recoverable backup. Agreement of three reviewers plus an independent probe raises the confidence.
findings.x-fix: Fail closed in key() (and ideally the metadata path schema) for any segment ending in "." or " " or matching an 8.3 "~<digit>" form, or key existing metadata entries via realpath relative to the real root. Add refusal rows for these spellings to the alias matrix for do_not_read (file and directory prefix), manifest and lock entries, asserting no writes.
findings.x-resolution: T045/T046: key() rejects trailing-dot/trailing-space segments and ~digit spellings before protection lookup or reads; safePath shares this check. Exact dot segments remain canonicalized for F22. Metadata failures identify both the bad spelling and declaring source. The 60-row matrix covers six spellings across feature/quick exclusions, backup/candidate exclusions, excluded read_first/artifacts, managed files/markers, locks and nested contract directory prefixes. Unsafe directory cases also refuse usage reports. Every preview/apply asserts exact diagnostics and unchanged snapshots.
findings.x-rereview: Round 4 verified: key() rejects trailing-dot, trailing-space and ~digit segments before lookup/read (context-guards.mjs:33-44) and safePath shares it (L71); every metadata caller passes its declaring source (L173/193/200/223). Independent probes refused CLI and metadata aliases with no writes. Over-broad ~digit matching of legitimate long names tracked separately as F38.

findings.x-fix: Add unexcluded case-variant read_first (no sha) and artifact (sha via hashArtifact) rows asserting preview allowed:false with reasons exactly ["Target is read_first, source/hash-bound or managed"] and the same E_CONTEXT_PROTECTED apply refusal with unchanged snapshots. Optionally add a ~2 short-name spelling and a .baton/lock.json declaring source.
findings.x-resolution: T051 adds four unexcluded rows: uppercase full path and mixed-case leaf, each with checksum-free read_first or hashArtifact-bound artifact. Exact preview reason array and apply message/file/code assert the binding cause, with immediate no-write snapshots. Case-variant files are materialized so the same test exercises binding rather than missing-source errors on case-sensitive hosts.

Focused suite green.

findings.title: ~digit alias rule refuses legitimate long names, aborting usage/scope and all context commands
findings.reason: key() treats any segment containing ~<digit> as an 8.3 alias (L35-36). contextFilePaths passes every readdir entry to contextExcluded/key (L362), but readdir returns real long names, so a legitimate specs/<feature>/notes~2.md or contracts/draft~1/ makes usage/scope/concise throw Unsafe context path for the whole feature instead of listing it (adversarial persona reproduced; removing the file restored output). Likewise a schema-valid handoff/lock path such as docs/v~2-notes.md (handoff/lock path patterns accept ~) or a quick baton named fix~1.md blocks every context command repo-wide. Fails closed, so not a protection bypass, but it contradicts the accepted schema and spec usage reporting for valid feature trees.
findings.x-severity: adversarial-reviewer rated both instances P3 (0.85, 0.75); merged.
findings.x-fix: Narrow the short-name check to the generated 8.3 shape (e.g. /^[^.~]{1,6}~\d{1,6}(\.[^.]{0,3})?$/i) or exempt readdir-derived canonical names; keep metadata trailing-dot/space rejection. Add tests: a legitimate research~2.md in the feature tree still appears in usage/scope, and a schema-valid long ~digit metadata path does not disable context commands, while 002-DR~1/SPEC~1.MD aliases still refuse.
findings.x-resolution: T052 limits extra validation to genuine 8.3-shaped components with at most eight base characters, then uses safePath real-path identity to distinguish an actual canonical tilde-number name from an alias. Lexical keys retain dot/space/root rejection but no longer reject ordinary readdir names merely for containing ~digit. checkedKey preserves declaring-source errors for unresolved/aliased metadata and unsafe CLI candidates. New coverage reports research~2.md and contracts/draft~1/api.md, accepts long-name and literal SPEC~1.MD metadata in handoff/manifest/lock plus a fix~1.md quick baton, and exercises scope/usage/concise/compact preview without writes. The existing 60-row alias matrix remains green. Pre-fix new tests: five pass, one canonical-name regression fails; final focused acceptance:139/139.
findings.x-rereview: Round 5 verified for the reported scope: research~2.md and contracts/draft~1/api.md appear in scope/usage, long-name and literal SPEC~1.MD metadata no longer abort context commands, and real generated 8.3 aliases still refuse on an 8.3-enabled volume. The narrowed trigger regex introduced a new exclusion bypass for long names containing ~ (F39) and still blocks report-only commands for absent short-shaped entries (F40); both tracked separately against T052.

findings.title: 8.3 alias of a long name containing ~ bypasses checkedKey, so do_not_read declared by that alias does not exclude the canonical file
findings.reason: checkedKey only runs the safePath/realpath identity check when a segment matches /^[^.~]{1,6}~\d{1,6}(?:\.[^.]{0,3})?$/i. Windows preserves ~ from the long name when generating short names, so a~b-long-name.md gets the generated alias A~B-LO~1.MD (two tildes), which the [^.~] prefix rejects. The alias is then keyed lexically as drafts/a~b-lo~1.md and never equals the canonical key, so contextExcluded misses the canonical file. Orchestrator reproduced on an 8.3-enabled os.tmpdir volume: do_not_read [drafts/A~B-LO~1.MD]; --candidate drafts/A~B-LO~1.MD previews refused as excluded, but --candidate drafts/a~b-long-name.md previews allowed:true and --expect/--apply exit 0 wrote the excluded bytes into specs/002-draft/spec.md. The persona also observed scope reading and counting an excluded feature file declared via such an alias (FR-016). Round-4 code rejected these segments lexically, so this is a regression introduced by T052; it violates FR-007/FR-008 exclusion fail-closed semantics in the same class as F32.
findings.x-severity: adversarial-reviewer rated P1 (0.9); synthesized P2 to match F32 (same alias-exclusion bypass class, requires an alias-spelled declaration, exclusion-only because contextTarget names cannot contain ~).
findings.x-fix: Trigger the filesystem identity check for any existing segment that could be a generated short name regardless of preceding characters (e.g. any segment containing ~ followed by digits, or simply canonicalize every existing metadata/candidate path through safePath/realpath before keying), keeping fail-closed on identity mismatch. Add a Windows regression that creates a long name containing ~ (e.g. drafts/a~b-long-name.md and a feature-tree file), reads its generated alias via dir /x, declares the alias in do_not_read, and asserts the canonical candidate is refused with exact reason/no writes and scope/usage omit the excluded file; skip with an explicit reason only when no short name is generated. Have the existing short-name matrix rows assert the alias exists on Windows hosts (or skip) so the realpath identity branch, not ENOENT, is what is under test.
findings.x-resolution: T054/T056: every existing metadata reference now passes safePath identity checks, independent of filename heuristics, with normalized lexical metadata syntax and declaring-source diagnostics. Candidate short-name checks also accept arbitrary prefixes before ~digit. The new Windows regression obtains the generated A~B-LO~1.MD alias through cmd's short-name expansion, proves it exists, is not a symbolic link and resolves to the same file, and asserts exact metadata refusal in compact preview/apply and scope/usage with null report data and unchanged snapshots. The ten matrix short-name rows now obtain and prove real generated aliases too. The owner explicitly approved unsupported-platform handling while keeping all safety assertions and AC-US2-2 mandatory. Both new behavioral tests failed before the guard change; all 63 selected identity/matrix tests and all 140 registered acceptance tests passed afterward without skips on this Windows filesystem. Independent verification remains required.
findings.x-rereview: Verified round 6: orchestrator reproduced the original round-5 scenario with real generated aliases and found refusal with no writes; adversarial and testing personas independently confirmed; focused 142/142 with 0 skips.

findings.title: Absent short-shaped metadata entry (e.g. do_not_read notes~1.md) aborts report-only scope/usage for every feature
findings.reason: checkedKey converts ENOENT from safePath into Unsafe context metadata path for any segment matching the short-name shape. A schema-valid do_not_read naming a not-yet-created legitimate file such as notes~1.md (or ABSENT~1.MD, probed) therefore makes contextProtection throw, so scope, usage and optimize reports fail repo-wide, including on Linux where no 8.3 aliasing exists. A path that does not resolve cannot alias any existing file at evaluation time, so this over-refusal protects nothing; FR-008 requires fail-closed for mutation, and F38 required legitimate tilde-number names not to disable context commands. No test pins the intended policy (the canonical test uses v~3-absent.md, which does not match the shape).
findings.x-severity: adversarial-reviewer rated P3 (0.65); testing-reviewer independently flagged the missing absent short-shaped do_not_read coverage (0.6); merged with agreement boost.
findings.x-fix: Treat ENOENT from the identity check as "no alias possible" and key the path lexically (still rejecting dot/space/root/colon spellings and non-ENOENT errors), or explicitly document and test a different intended policy. Add tests for an absent short-shaped do_not_read entry and an existing literal SPEC~1.MD in do_not_read asserting scope/usage behaviour and exclusion of a candidate bound by it.
findings.x-resolution: T055/T056: only ENOENT during metadata identity discovery preserves the normalized lexical key; existing aliases, unsafe syntax and other filesystem failures remain non-success. Required read_first/artifact content still must exist and satisfy its binding, and missing short-shaped CLI candidates retain their strict refusal. The regression proves ABSENT~1.MD is absent and excludes a real literal LITERA~1.MD containing invalid UTF-8. Scope/usage omit both while preserving exclusions, concise remains session-only, all three optimize reports stay report-only, an ordinary draft candidate remains eligible and the excluded literal candidate refuses preview/apply before decoding. Snapshots remain unchanged. Documentation states the absent-metadata versus required-source boundary. Owner approval of corrected real-alias fixtures was recorded without waiving AC-US2-2; independent verification remains required.
findings.x-rereview: Verified round 6: orchestrator reproduced the original round-5 scenario with real generated aliases and found refusal with no writes; adversarial and testing personas independently confirmed; focused 142/142 with 0 skips.

findings.title: 8.3-shaped --candidate is filesystem-checked before the exclusion check, so preview throws instead of returning an excluded reason
findings.reason: Dismissed: fails closed with no write, and the CLI candidate contract established for F35/F36 (test "context protection labels unsafe CLI candidate paths", docs/06 candidate guidance) deliberately reports unresolved or aliased short-shaped candidates as Unsafe context path in both preview and apply. Folding it into reasons would change an asserted diagnostic contract for no safety benefit.

findings.title: Non-ENOENT filesystem errors on any metadata reference now crash report-only context commands as raw E_INTERNAL
findings.reason: T056 routes every manifest/handoff/lock reference through safePath, but checkedKey still rethrows any error that is neither ENOENT nor BatonError. An excluded path the user cannot stat (e.g. do_not_read secrets/prod.env under a directory with a deny ACL, or a POSIX directory without search permission) now makes scope, usage and optimize run exit 10 with E_INTERNAL and an absolute-path message, where bb0232e returned exit 0. It still fails closed (no write), so FR-008 holds, but report-only commands lose the source-labelled diagnostic required by FR-017 and the T056/F40 intent that exclusion-only metadata not abort reports. Reproduced by the adversarial persona via icacls deny; confirmed by code reading of checkedKey L54-60.
findings.x-fix: Convert non-ENOENT filesystem errors from metadata identity checks into a BatonError that names the declaring source (e.g. Unsafe context metadata path ... declared by <source> with the errno reason) so mutation stays fail-closed and reports fail with a protected, diagnosable error; or explicitly treat EACCES/EPERM on exclusion-only (do_not_read) metadata as the lexical key, keeping read_first/artifact/manifest/lock strict. Add a regression asserting exact code/message/file and unchanged snapshot (chmod 000 parent on POSIX, deny ACL or injected error on Windows).
findings.x-resolution: T058/T060 retain fail-closed behavior and convert metadata filesystem failures to E_CONTEXT_PROTECTED/exit1 with the declaring source and errno code, without including the raw absolute-path error. Portable node:test mocks inject EACCES, EPERM and ENAMETOOLONG into lstat only for the excluded path; exact code, exit, relative source, message and unchanged snapshots are asserted. Builtin ESM bindings are restored in finally. No operating-system permissions are changed. All three injected cases failed on raw errno codes before correction and now pass; independent verification remains required.
findings.x-rereview: Verified round 7: non-ENOENT metadata errors yield source-labelled E_CONTEXT_PROTECTED with errno, no absolute path, snapshots unchanged (EACCES/EPERM/ENAMETOOLONG injected).

findings.title: No regression pins identity checks for linked metadata; reverting checkedKey to the ~digit trigger passes the suite
findings.reason: Every metadata-refusal assertion uses a ~digit spelling, trailing dot/space or root alias, so changing `source || /~\d/.test(path)` back to the tilde heuristic (or dropping the identity call for non-tilde metadata) would not fail any test on Windows or Linux. The round-6 change also closes a pre-existing do_not_read bypass (adversarial persona: at bb0232e a junction vendor -> vendor-real excluded via do_not_read vendor allowed compact --candidate vendor-real/x.md; HEAD refuses), but nothing guards that closure. Additionally shortAlias skips before asserting the base path exists, so a fixture mistake converts mandatory AC-US2-2 rows into silent skips.
findings.x-fix: Add a platform-independent test where do_not_read (and one manifest/read_first entry) names a junction/directory-symlink and a hardlinked file; assert exact E_CONTEXT_PROTECTED Unsafe context metadata path ... declared by <source>, file=source, null data and unchanged snapshot for compact preview/apply and scope/usage, plus a junction-target candidate refusal. In shortAlias, lstat the base path before invoking cmd so missing fixtures fail rather than skip.
findings.x-resolution: T059 adds plain-name directory-junction/symlink, hardlink and file-symlink metadata cases for both handoff do_not_read and manifest ownership. Exact source-labelled refusals, null report data and snapshots are checked for compact preview/apply and scope/usage with the canonical junction-target file as candidate. File symlink cases were initially registered as conditional on platform permission support; this Windows host runs both junction/hardlink sources and explicitly skips the two unsupported file-symlink cases. Existing real 8.3 rows still execute, not skip. shortAlias now lstats its canonical base before any platform/8.3 skip; a portable noSkip regression failed before that fix and passes afterward. Plain linked-path checks already passed before this correction, so no false red claim is made. Full protection selector: 135 tests, 133 pass, 2 explicit permission skips, 0 failures; independent verification remains required.
findings.x-rereview: Verified round 7: plain-name junction/hardlink metadata refusals for handoff and manifest pass and fail under the reverted trigger; shortAlias lstat precedes skip.

findings.title: Hardlinked, junction or file-component metadata references now abort report-only commands
findings.reason: Dismissed: these refusals fail closed and match the approved contract. FR-008 requires unreadable/ambiguous protection metadata to fail closed, the spec edge case requires links/junctions not to evade protection, and docs/06 states linked or aliased paths are not trusted metadata. Unlike F40 (an absent path that cannot alias anything), a linked or hardlinked exclusion names real bytes reachable through another spelling; the junction case demonstrably closes a bypass that existed at bb0232e. A path through a regular-file component is malformed metadata. Richer dual-key exclusion semantics would be a contract change for the owner, not a review fix. Diagnostic quality is covered by F42.

findings.title: No CI job executes the real-alias AC-US2-2/F39 rows
findings.reason: Dismissed: the repository owner explicitly approved real-alias fixtures with skips only where real 8.3 aliases are unavailable (recorded baton question answered Keep requirement); Linux CI cannot generate them, and adding Windows CI jobs is new CI scope outside the approved plan. AC-US2-2 remains mandatory and was verified independently in this checkout on Windows with 0 skips. The silent-skip-on-missing-fixture weakness is captured in F43.
